title: B2B affiliate recruitment: respond fast, measure influence, coach partners
summary: Final part of Dustin Howes's series on building a B2B affiliate program from scratch. He argues for instant follow-up when an affiliate says yes, attribution that captures both influence and conversion, and hands-on coaching of partners who promote but don't convert.

principles.text: When an affiliate says yes to recruitment, get on the call immediately; speed to lead decides whether interest survives.
principles.quote: Speed to lead is everything in affiliate recruitment.

principles.text: Interest decays within a day or two; delay means the affiliate has moved on.
principles.quote: Wait a day or two and that interest is already gone. They've moved on with their life.

principles.text: Your tech stack must measure influence and conversions together; last-touch attribution misleads and leads to bad cuts.
principles.quote: if you cannot measure influence and conversions at the same time, you're dead. Last-touch attribution will lie to you.

principles.text: Don't cut a channel just because it shows few last-touch conversions; understand its role in the buying journey first.
principles.quote: One brand killed their Facebook ads because conversions looked low. Sales dropped 25%.

principles.text: Coach partners who promote but don't convert: find where they're stuck and give them angles that work.
principles.quote: If someone is promoting but not converting, hop on a call. See where they're getting stuck. Give them the angles that work.

principles.text: Affiliate marketing is a relationship business, so invest in personal contact with partners.
